samples: This program offers an agent-callable tool that converts a decimal amount from one three-letter currency code to another. It looks up today's rate from the Frankfurter exchange-rate service and returns the result rounded to cents. It is limited to network access to that one host, and it fails with a distinct error if the service is unreachable, returns unreadable data, or has no rate for the requested pair. Because the rate is fetched live on every call with no caching, you depend on that third-party service being available.

This module offers one function, published as a tool for agents, that converts an amount from one three-letter currency code to another using today's rate from the Frankfurter exchange-rate web service, rounded to two decimal places. It is limited to network access to that one host. It fails with a specific "rate unavailable" error if the service has no rate for the pair, and passes on any HTTP or JSON-parsing errors. Before relying on it, note that it always rounds to cents, which may not suit currencies with other minor-unit conventions, and that it does no validation of the amount itself.

This program offers a single tool that converts an amount from one currency to another using today's rate from the Frankfurter exchange-rate service, rounded to cents. Currency codes must be three uppercase letters, and the tool fails with a specific error if the service has no rate for the requested pair, or with a network or JSON-parsing error if the lookup itself goes wrong. It is allowed network access only to that one host and does nothing else (no files, no console), so it is narrow in what it can touch and is published to agents as a callable tool.

This program exposes a single tool that agents can call to convert a money amount from one currency to another. It looks up today's exchange rate from the Frankfurter web service and returns the converted amount rounded to cents. It can only make network requests to that one host, it fails with a distinct error if the service has no rate for the pair, and it also fails if the HTTP request or JSON parsing fails. Currency codes are checked only for being three uppercase letters, not for being real ISO codes, so a made-up code would reach the service and come back as an error.

This program offers one agent-callable tool that converts an amount from one currency to another at today's rate, rounded to cents. It checks that both currencies are three-letter uppercase codes, then makes a single request to the Frankfurter exchange-rate service, the only network access it is allowed. It can fail if the request fails, if the response isn't valid JSON, or if the service returns no rate for the requested pair, and each case is reported as a distinct error.
